about: The Blender half of the mapping table: every Blender property the perturbation sweep (tools/io_sync/perturb.py) changes, and what the X3D 4.0 export does with it. Classes: carried (written faithfully), approximated (written through a lossy conversion), clamped (written within a range, cut outside it), dropped (affects Blender's render or data, not written), editor_only (no effect on any render). A row with a receipt rule puts an entry in the loss receipt (source/receipt.py) whenever the rule fires for an exported datablock. Grades: Confirmed = the sweep observed the behaviour the class claims; Likely = observed inert, class by reading Blender's and X3D's documentation; Suspected = the probe cannot exercise it.

classes.carried: the export writes it, and a change changes the file
classes.approximated: the export writes it through a conversion that loses information
classes.clamped: the export writes it inside a range and cuts it outside
classes.dropped: it changes what Blender renders or stores, and the export does not write it
classes.editor_only: it changes no render: viewport, UI, selection, bookkeeping

versions: a row's "before": {"5.0": {...}} replaces its fields on Blender versions before 5.0 (the sweep found world nodes switchable on 4.5 LTS and always on in 5.x)

receipt_rules.neq: an entry when the value differs from neutral (Blender's default)
receipt_rules.gt: an entry when the value is above value
receipt_rules.always: an entry for every exported datablock the row applies to
receipt_rules.when: the rule applies only when another property of the same datablock is in the list
receipt_rules.unless_custom: no entry when the datablock carries this custom property (the import kept the file's value)

probe.scope: the probe's datablocks only (v3 plan stop rule): object, mesh, material and its Principled BSDF, camera, world and its Background, four light types
